subject: P50/P95 measurement interpretation and grace calibration for Hosted API
messages:
From: Sam Wells <sam.wells@brightline.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Hosted API p50/p95 commitments — clarification requested

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood's routing and caching features. Procurement had a couple of questions before we sign the pilot MSA: we want to confirm exactly how you define p50 and p95 for the Hosted API (tokens vs. request end-to-end), and how the measurement window is applied (rolling minute, 5-minute epoch, etc.).

Specifically, our SRE wants to know:
- Do your p50/p95 numbers represent server-side processing only, or do they include network egress to client?
- What's the aggregation window (rolling or fixed bucket)?
- Are there carve-outs for burst traffic during scheduled onboarding runs?

I've attached the contract excerpt procurement is referencing. Can you send a short proposal we can attach to the MSA for the pilot (30–90 day onboarding) that outlines the measurement approach and any temporary grace periods?

Appreciate it — Sam

Attachment: brightline_contract_excerpt.pdf (PDF, 148 KB)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wells <sam.wells@brightline.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T11:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API p50/p95 commitments — clarification requested

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the clear list. Long story short: Redwood's hosted p50/p95 commitments are measured server-side (our edge + compute processing) and reported as request latency from our ingress to final token emission. They do not attempt to include the customer's last-mile network. A short proposal below that we can package as an addendum:

Proposed SLO language (pilot addendum) — Hosted API
- P50: <= 120 ms
- P95: <= 500 ms
- Measurement: rolling 5-minute window computed on successful requests, aggregated per-region (US-East, US-West) and reported in UTC
- Error handling: only successful responses (2xx) are included in latency percentiles; client timeouts and user aborts are excluded
- Carve-outs: scheduled maintenance windows (>= 15 minutes, pre-notified 48h) and bulk ingestion jobs (>10k tokens in a single request) are excluded from both numerator and denominator for the duration of the event.
- Pilot grace: for the first 30 days after cutover, Brightline will be eligible for a one-time 14-day temporary tolerance window where measured p95 may exceed target without SLA credit, provided we jointly run mitigation playbooks and provide evidence.

If you want the numbers tighter, we can propose region-specific baselines — e.g., p95=350ms for US-East — but the above is our standard hosted baseline suitable for multi-tenant capacity.

I'll loop in our contracts/ops folks if you want a formal PDF addendum.

Best,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0142

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API p50/p95 commitments — clarification requested

Rishi / Lauren —

Checking details before we send the addendum:
- Evidence package: procurement will likely ask for baseline slice data (per-route p50/p95 for 7 days) and sample traces. I'll prep the slo_evidence_template.xlsx and include 7-day rolling histograms.
- Measurement nuance: our current telemetry applies a rolling 5-minute window at the edge, but the persisted reports in Console are hourly rollups with per-minute granularity. For the contract we should specify both: rolling 5-minute for real-time alerts and 1-hour aggregated reporting for formal SLA measurement.
- Carveouts: recommend explicitly excluding retries where client behavior retried faster than our client-idempotency threshold. Also we should define 'bulk ingestion' as single requests with >10k tokens or >5000 tokens for non-streaming endpoints.

I'll attach the evidence template for Lauren to review. If all OK, let's include a short 'measurement appendix' clause in the addendum.

Attachment: slo_evidence_template.xlsx (XLSX, 54 KB)

- Karthik

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wells <sam.wells@brightline.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-04T14:18:00-04:00
Subject: Draft SLO addendum for Brightline pilot

Hi Sam —

Thanks — attached is a short addendum that mirrors the language Rishi proposed and includes a two-paragraph measurement appendix (rolling 5-minute window for alerting; hourly aggregates for billing/SLA calculations).

Key points called out in the draft:
- Explicit definition: latency = time from Redwood ingress receipt to final token emission (server-side).
- Reporting cadence: Console will show rolling 5-minute telemetry; contractual SLA evaluations will use hourly aggregates derived from those 1-minute samples.
- Pilot grace: 14-day tolerance window available once within the first 30 days; requires joint RCA and mitigation plan.
- Triggers for rollback: if broad p95 degradation (>=20% of routes) persists for 72 hours despite mitigation, Redwood will initiate capacity rebalancing or temporary routing to dedicated capacity.

Attachment: Brightline-SLO-Addendum-v1.pdf (PDF, 32 KB)

If this aligns with procurement's needs, we can route for signature (DocuSign) and include the evidence package after cutover.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success — Hosted
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: Sam Wells <sam.wells@brightline.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-06T08:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLO addendum for Brightline pilot

Lauren —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. The addendum looks good overall. Two small asks from our side before we sign:

1) Temporary onboarding uplift: during our initial traffic ramp (expected 7–30 days), we request a temporary p95 uplift to 700 ms for a period of up to 30 days with a joint mitigation plan. This will cover spikes while we optimize end-to-end prompt batching.
2) Measurement timezone and timestamps: please confirm all reported timestamps will be in UTC in both the Console and the formal hourly aggregate reports. Our SRE needs to align logs across CDN, app, and Redwood.

Also attaching a brief network topology so you can confirm there are no planned egress constraints that would affect measurements.

Attachment: network-topology.pdf (PDF, 88 KB)

If you can ack both items (and note the DocuSign route), procurement will greenlight sign-off.

—Sam

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wells <sam.wells@brightline.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-08T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLO addendum for Brightline pilot — agreed changes and next steps

Sam / team —

Confirmed and thanks for the clear asks. Agreed changes below, which we'll incorporate into the DocuSign-ready addendum:

- Temporary onboarding uplift: Approved. For onboarding ramp, Brightline will have a one-time 30-day uplift where p95 contract threshold is 700 ms. The uplift will be invoked once via an email to redwood-sla@redwood.ai and requires a joint mitigation plan (SRE runbook, expected telemetry collection).
- Timezone: All telemetry and hourly aggregate exports will be in UTC with ISO-8601 timestamps. Console will continue to present local-time views, but the export attached to the SLA evaluation will be UTC.
- Measurement specifics: Rolling 5-minute window for alerting; hourly aggregated SLA buckets derived from 1-minute samples for contractual evaluations. Successful responses only (2xx). We will explicitly exclude client-initiated aborts, documented bulk ingestion events (>10k tokens), and pre-notified maintenance >=15 minutes.

Next steps:
1) We'll update the PDF addendum to incorporate the uplift clause and timezone language and circulate a DocuSign envelope to the procurement contact (procurement@brightline.com) by EOD Thursday.
2) Karthik will prepare the 7-day baseline evidence package post-cutover and share the slo_evidence_template.xlsx for your team to review.
3) After signature, we'll schedule a 30-minute runbook walk-through with Brightline SREs to confirm instrumentation and alerts.

Thanks — excited to get Brightline into pilot.

Rishi
Head of Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference
